governingDocuments.AGENTS.md: The repository owner's standing branch policy and agent rules (also linked from CLAUDE.md) - read this before acting on anything in this file. Covers: development is the only branch to push to without explicit permission; main is only touched on explicit owner instruction, and only via the release branch + promote-release.yml, never a direct push; PR #11 (ci-monitor -> main) must never be merged or closed, backed by block-pr-7.yml's check and guard-ci-monitor-pr.yml's auto-reopen; the AI-to-AI handoff protocol requiring this file and DEVLOG.md to be updated together in every project commit, DEVLOG.md's chain-of-custody format (dev-plan reference + a Command log archive capped at 10 sessions and 180 days), the governingDocuments recheck rule after any 10+ minute idle gap; and the standing rule against invisible self-repair.
governingDocuments.DEVLOG.md: The chronological, per-commit development log, enforced as a chain of custody with two parts: 'Shared AI handoff' (current status, referencing the dev plan in this file's activePlan.currentPrompt/handoffNotes.completed/remaining) and 'Command log archive' (one '### Session:' entry per unit of work, newest first, capped at 10 sessions and a 180-day backup age limit). Read the Shared AI handoff section first, every time, per AGENTS.md's 'Read DEVLOG.md first, always' rule. This file (AI-HANDOFF.json) and DEVLOG.md must be updated together in the same commit; neither supersedes the other. See src/handoffPolicy.js for exactly how this is validated.
governingDocuments.AI-CONFLICTS.json: The auditable ledger of AI-agent conflicts (concurrent or contradictory work between agents), governed by templates/ai-conflict-resolution.md and enforced by .github/workflows/ai-conflict-governance.yml. Never delete, bypass, or disable it.
governingDocuments.CLAUDE.md: Claude-specific entry point; it just points to AGENTS.md, which applies to every AI agent working here, not only Claude.
governingDocuments.README.md: The project's own generated/maintained documentation of what The Crucible does, its CLI, and its workflow steps - kept in sync with source via npm run docs:sync/docs:check.
governingDocuments.templates/ai-conflict-resolution.md: The actual conflict-resolution procedure AGENTS.md and AI-CONFLICTS.json point to: freeze the contested mutation, preserve both sides in the shared handoff, and get an explicit owner decision instead of silently picking a side.
governingDocuments.templates/required-check-rollout.md: The rollout plan AGENTS.md requires for any new required workflow check: report-only on development first, then explicit owner promotion, then npm run audit:required-check, before it is ever added to branch protection or a ruleset. Directly relevant to how `block` must be added as a required check on main.
governingDocuments.templates/agent-boundaries.md: The AI-agent rules for this repository's one-way link to adopter projects that pin The Crucible as a security gate - what an agent may and may not do when investigating a Crucible-related CI failure in a project that consumes this repository.
governingDocuments.src/handoffPolicy.js: The code that actually enforces the AI-to-AI handoff protocol and DEVLOG.md's chain-of-custody requirement, run by the AI handoff policy CI check: validateHandoffPlan (this file's activePlan/handoffNotes must contain, among other fields, a non-empty currentPrompt) and validateDevlogChainOfCustody (DEVLOG.md's Shared AI handoff section must reference this file's dev plan, and its Command log archive must hold 1-10 '### Session:' entries, none older than 180 days, with the newest having a start/finish pair). Read this to know exactly what is technically verified, not just what AGENTS.md describes in prose.

sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session, no matter which agent or tool is running it, and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt below - even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation. Branch policy, PR locks (e.g. PR #11), and handoff state can all change while an agent is idle; a long gap is treated the same as a fresh session. See AGENTS.md's 'Recheck governingDocuments at the start of every session' rule.

activePlan.objective: Per the owner's explicit request: cap DEVLOG.md's Command log so it doesn't grow unbounded, using a hybrid design - keep only the 10 most recent sessions inline, with a 180-day age limit as a backup in case the count cap alone proves too strict or too loose.
activePlan.currentPrompt: if the 10-session cap with real CI enforcement gets to be to much limit it to within 180 days as a back up system
steps: Restructure DEVLOG.md into two parts: Shared AI handoff (current status only) and a new Command log archive section holding one ### Session: entry per unit of work, newest first.

Update AGENTS.md's 'DEVLOG.md is a chain of custody' section and all affected tests (test/handoffPolicy.test.js, test/workflow.test.js) for the new two-part structure and dual cap.
Run the full local suite plus every fast/offline audit before pushing.
